summary: NOT IN tests whether a value is absent from a set.
syntax: expression NOT IN (SELECT expression FROM table WHERE expression IS NOT NULL)
documentation: NOT IN tests whether a value is absent from a set. SQL uses three-valued logic: a NULL on the right can make a nonmatching comparison unknown rather than true. Filtering NULLs from the subquery makes an exclusion list useful for known identifiers.
returns: Unblocked non-NULL product ids in ascending order.
caution: Decide the intended treatment of NULL on both sides explicitly. A NULL left operand needs its own exclusion condition, including when the right-hand set is empty.
scenarios: Exclude suppressed product identifiers from a local catalog export.
Remove blocked customer ids from a report preview.
Filter a staging list against an exclusion list with missing values.
title: Exclude known blocked identifiers
problem: Return non-NULL products.id absent from blocked.product_id. Ignore NULL entries in blocked. Preserve product duplicates and sort ascending by id.
goal: Use NOT IN with NULL filtering or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Filter NULLs in the subquery and guard products.id explicitly.
